```{r}
#| label: setup
#| include: false
suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(tidyverse)
  library(brms)
  library(posterior)
})
source("R/01_prepare_data.R")
source("R/02_fit_models.R")
source("R/theme_jama.R"); source("R/06_sensitivity_models.R")

xlsx <- "data/TTP_MetaAnalysis_Extraction_Complete_v4.xlsx"
prim_dir <- "_brms_cache/primary"
sens_dir <- "_brms_cache/sensitivity"

es_all  <- prepare_effect_sizes(xlsx, include_inclusive_pool = FALSE, drop_contaminated_ttp = TRUE)
es_mort <- es_for_outcome(es_all, "mortality")
es_inc  <- prepare_effect_sizes(xlsx, include_inclusive_pool = TRUE,  drop_contaminated_ttp = TRUE) |>
  es_for_outcome("mortality")

tbl_study <- readxl::read_excel(xlsx, sheet = "tbl_study")
tbl_pop   <- readxl::read_excel(xlsx, sheet = "tbl_population")
tbl_ttp   <- readxl::read_excel(xlsx, sheet = "tbl_ttp")
tbl_out   <- readxl::read_excel(xlsx, sheet = "tbl_outcomes")

bib_keys <- sub("^@[A-Za-z]+\\{([^,]+),.*", "\\1", grep("^@", readLines("references.bib"), value = TRUE))
fit_path <- function(name, dir = prim_dir) file.path(dir, paste0(name, ".rds"))
read_fit <- function(name, dir = prim_dir) readRDS(fit_path(name, dir))
fmt_n    <- function(x) format(x, big.mark = ",")
# Pipe table with relative column widths (pandoc reads widths from the separator row)
tab <- function(x, w = NULL, ...) {
  k <- as.character(knitr::kable(x, format = "pipe", ...))
  if (!is.null(w)) {
    stopifnot(length(w) == ncol(x))
    k[2] <- paste0("|", paste0(":", strrep("-", pmax(3, round(100 * w / sum(w)))), collapse = "|"), "|")
  }
  knitr::asis_output(paste(c("", k, ""), collapse = "\n"))
}

# Studies with a bib entry are cited; the rest are given as author and year
study_label <- function(id, author, year) {
  ifelse(id %in% bib_keys, paste0(author, " ", year, " [@", id, "]"), paste(author, year))
}
```

# 1. Search strategy

## 1.1 Search parameters

| Field | Content |
|:-----------------------|:---------------------------------------------------------------|
| Sources searched | MEDLINE (PubMed), Embase (Elsevier), Scopus (Elsevier), Web of Science Core Collection (Clarivate) and Cochrane CENTRAL (Wiley Cochrane Library) |
| Search date | All sources were searched on May 22, 2026, from database inception |
| Date and language limits | None at the search level |
| Filters | No methodological or publication-type filter was applied to the Embase, Scopus, Web of Science or CENTRAL strategies. See section 1.3 for the PubMed strategy. |
| Concept blocks | The Embase, Scopus and Web of Science strategies combined a time-to-positivity block with one or more clinical-outcome blocks (shock, mortality, sepsis, prognosis, outcome assessment). The protocol specified no outcome block, so adding one was a deviation that may have reduced sensitivity. The wording of each block differs between sources, as shown below. |
| Records | 6,014 records identified across the five sources; 1,409 duplicates removed automatically in Covidence (none manually); 4,605 records entered screening. A further 1,351 of those were subsequently identified as duplicate records that Covidence had not detected, leaving 3,254 unique records (table 2) |
| De-duplication | Covidence (automatic), supplemented after export by exact matching on normalised title |
| Selection route | Covidence was used for de-duplication only; no title and abstract screening was recorded in it. Screening was performed by the staged automated procedure described in section 1.8, which identified 355 reports sought for full-text review. Every one of those 355 reports is present in the database export, so no record reached full text from a source other than the five databases. |
| Baseline studies | The 57 studies carried forward from the earlier (thesis) review were identified by that review and were not re-screened here. Two of them (Alvarez 2012 and Peri 2026) were identified by hand-searching at that time. |

: Search parameters. {#tbl-search-params}

## 1.3 PubMed (MEDLINE)

\[**Unresolved — confirm against the PubMed search history before submission.**\] Two different
PubMed strategies are recorded in the project and they are not interchangeable. The strategy
reproduced below as (a) is the one previously reported as executed. The strategy reproduced as
(b) was designed on May 12, 2026 after a documented relative-recall exercise, and the record
favours (b) as the strategy actually run on May 22: (b) was counted at 1,245 hits on May 12,
Covidence imported 1,250 PubMed records on May 22, and re-running (b) today with those date
limits returns 1,266 and 1,272 respectively — a constant offset consistent with retrospective
MEDLINE indexing, with an increment between the two dates of +6 against the +5 recorded. Strategy
(a) returns 55 records at the search date. Resolve which was run, retain that one here, and
delete the other.

**(a) Three-block strategy, as previously reported**

```
(((("time to positivity") OR ("time to culture positivity")) OR ("time to blood culture positivity"))
 AND
 (("Shock, Septic"[Mesh]) OR ("Mortality"[Mesh]) OR ("Sepsis"[Mesh]))
 AND
 (("Prognosis"[Mesh]) OR ("Outcome Assessment, Health Care"[Mesh]))
)
```

The second and third blocks carry no free-text equivalents, so any record not yet MeSH-indexed
under those headings is unreachable; this disproportionately removes recently published papers.

**(b) Two-block strategy (population AND exposure, no outcome block), consistent with the protocol**

```
(
  "Blood Culture"[Mesh] OR "Bacteremia"[Mesh] OR "Fungemia"[Mesh]
  OR "Candidemia"[Mesh] OR "Sepsis"[Mesh]
  OR "Bacteraemi*"[tiab] OR "Bacteremi*"[tiab]
  OR "Fungaemi*"[tiab] OR "Fungemi*"[tiab]
  OR "Candidaemi*"[tiab] OR "Candidemi*"[tiab]
  OR "Blood culture"[tiab] OR "Blood cultures"[tiab]
  OR "Bloodstream infection"[tiab] OR "Bloodstream infections"[tiab]
  OR "Blood stream infection"[tiab] OR "Blood stream infections"[tiab]
  OR "BSI"[tiab] OR "BSIs"[tiab]
)
AND
(
    "time to positivity"[tiab] OR "time-to-positivity"[tiab]
  OR "time to blood culture positivity"[tiab]
  OR "time to culture positivity"[tiab]
  OR "blood culture positivity"[tiab]
  OR "culture positivity"[tiab]
  OR "time to detection"[tiab] OR "time-to-detection"[tiab]
  OR "time to growth"[tiab]
  OR "time to positive"[tiab]
  OR "growth detection time"[tiab]
  OR "differential time to positivity"[tiab]
  OR "DTP"[tiab] OR "DTTP"[tiab]
  OR ( "TTP"[tiab]
       AND ("blood culture"[tiab] OR "blood cultures"[tiab]
            OR bacter*emi*[tiab] OR bloodstream[tiab]) )
  OR "bacteremia duration"[tiab] OR "bacteraemia duration"[tiab]
  OR "duration of bacteremia"[tiab] OR "duration of bacteraemia"[tiab]
)
NOT (animals[MeSH Terms] NOT humans[MeSH Terms])
```

Strategy (b) applies a human filter, so the "no methodological filter" statement in table 1 would
need qualifying if (b) is confirmed. Measured against the 125 included studies that are indexed in
PubMed, strategy (b) retrieves 121 (97%) and strategy (a) retrieves 38 (30%); because four terms in
(b) were added after inspecting earlier misses, its recall is not an entirely independent estimate.

```
("time to positivity") OR ("time to blood culture positivity") OR ("time to culture positivity")

```

## 1.8 Screening and prioritisation methods

Title and abstract screening was performed by a staged automated procedure. Covidence was used
for de-duplication only; no screening decisions were recorded in it.

**Stage 1 — deterministic keyword classification.** Every record was classified by a rule set
(`scripts/tier_new_papers.py`, reproduced in the data deposit) that matched title and abstract
against a time-to-positivity concept block and a bloodstream-infection concept block. The
time-to-positivity block allowed up to five intervening words (so that, for example, "time to
blood culture positivity" and "time to first positivity" both match) and included the
differential-time-to-positivity and growth-detection forms. A homonym filter suppressed records
in which "TTP" denoted thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura, TTP/HUS, ADAMTS13, plasma exchange,
time to progression, or the total testing process. Records were assigned to five tiers:

| Tier | Definition | Records |
|:---|:---|---:|
| 1 | Explicit time-to-positivity phrase and a blood-culture concept | 1,017 |
| 2 | "TTP" abbreviation and a blood-culture concept, homonyms removed | 23 |
| 3 | Blood-culture concept only, no time-to-positivity signal | 1,928 |
| 4 | Time-to-positivity signal only, no blood-culture concept | 118 |
| 5 | Neither concept | 1,097 |

: Keyword tier assignment of the 4,183 records remaining after matching against the earlier review. Counts are of records as exported; because tiering used whatever title and abstract each record carried, duplicate records of the same report could be tiered differently, and a report was treated as carrying a signal if any of its records did. On that basis the 1,017 tier-1 records correspond to 794 unique reports, and tiers 1 and 2 together to 814. {#tbl-tiers}

**Stage 2 — large language model adjudication of tier 3.** Tier-3 records carry blood-culture
content but no detected time-to-positivity signal, which may still be discussed in the body of the
paper. For tier-3 records with a retrievable PubMed abstract, a large language model read the
abstract and judged whether time to positivity was discussed. 299 records were assessed; 146 were
reclassified as carrying a signal and 153 were confirmed off-topic. Each decision is stored with a
written rationale and is provided in the data deposit.

**Stage 3 — relevance triage.** Records carrying a time-to-positivity signal were triaged for
relevance to the review question, separating studies in which time to positivity is a clinical
predictor from blood-culture system, bottle and media comparisons in which it is a laboratory
performance endpoint. This stage classified the 146 records promoted at stage 2, of which 101 were
judged off-topic and 45 were prioritised for full-text review, of which 44 entered the screening
pool; the remaining report (growth in anaerobic bottles as a predictor of mortality in
*Pseudomonas aeruginosa* bloodstream infection) was dropped without a recorded reason and was not
assessed. Stage 3 did not individually classify the records already in tier 1 before stage 2. Of
814 unique records carrying a time-to-positivity signal, 144 reached full-text review and 670 were
deferred without an individual eligibility decision. Of those 670, 142 report a clinical outcome
in their title or abstract; excluding paediatric and neonatal populations leaves 88 that meet the
population and outcome criteria on the face of the record and were never assessed. They are listed in the data deposit and reported as a
limitation in the main text.

**Composition of the 355 reports sought for full text.** The two routes overlap, and most of the
reports that reached full text had no time-to-positivity signal detectable by the keyword rule
set:

| How the record reached full-text review | Reports |
|:---------------------------------------------------------------|--------:|
| Time-to-positivity signal together with a blood-culture concept (tiers 1–2) | 144 |
| Tiered, but no time-to-positivity signal together with a blood-culture concept (tiers 3–5) | 142 |
| Never tiered: matched a study in the earlier review, or flagged for manual checking | 69 |
| **Total** | **355** |

: The 355 reports sought for full text, by what the keyword rule set had identified. The 142 tiered without a signal comprise 125 in tier 3, 5 in tier 4 and 12 in tier 5. By retrieval route the same 355 comprise 311 surfaced only by the semantic ranking, 32 only by keyword tiering and relevance triage, and 12 by both. {#tbl-selection-route}

**Prioritisation with a semantic search tool.** An AI-assisted semantic search tool (Elicit,
elicit.com) was used in parallel to rank the same literature against a natural-language statement
of the review question. All 355 reports that the combined routes sent to full-text review are
present in the database export (333 matched on DOI and the remaining 22 on normalised title), so
the tool identified no record that the five database searches had not already retrieved. It did,
however, perform most of the selection: of the 355 reports sent to full text, only 144 carried a
time-to-positivity signal that the keyword rule set had identified (@tbl-selection-route). It is therefore reported as a prioritisation aid and is not shown
as an information source in the study-flow diagram in the main text. The question entered was whether time to positivity predicts the risk of antibiotic
failure in adults with blood-culture-confirmed bloodstream infection, with persistent bacteremia,
relapse or recurrence, microbiological clearance, and all-cause mortality as outcomes.

**Full-text assessment.** The 302 reports assessed at full text were evaluated by a large language
model agent working from the full-text PDFs against the written eligibility criteria, with a
decision and a specific reason recorded for every report. The complete record is provided in the
data deposit. No dual independent human screening was performed and inter-rater agreement was not
assessed.

## 1.9 Strategies specified in the protocol but not run

CINAHL Complete (EBSCOhost), ClinicalTrials.gov, WHO ICTRP, medRxiv and bioRxiv were listed in the protocol but not searched, and forward citation tracking and reference-list searching were not performed. The CINAHL strategy that had been prepared is given for transparency.

```
(((MH "Outcome Assessment") OR (MH "Fatal Outcome") OR (MH "Treatment Outcomes"))
 OR ((MH "Prognosis") OR (MH "Clinical Assessment Tools"))
 OR ((MH "Mortality") OR (MH "Maternal Mortality") OR (MH "Hospital Mortality") OR (MH "Child Mortality") OR (MH "Infant Mortality"))
 OR ((MH "Neonatal Sepsis") OR (MH "Sepsis") OR (MH "Systemic Inflammatory Response Syndrome") OR (MH "Fungemia") OR (MH "Bacteremia"))
)
 AND
 (TX "time to positivity" OR TX "time to blood culture positivity" OR TX "time to culture positivity"
  OR "persistent bacteremia")
```

# Overview

This appendix accompanies the main manuscript and gives the search strategy (section 1), details of the included studies (section 2), model specification (section 3), model fit, diagnostics, and convergence (section 4), sensitivity analyses (section 5), and reproducibility and the software and R packages used (sections 6 and 7). All numbers are generated from the extraction workbook (`data/TTP_MetaAnalysis_Extraction_Complete_v4.xlsx`) and the cached `brms` fits in the project repository.

The **primary pool** comprises `{r} attr(es_all, "n_studies")` studies meeting the strict eligibility criterion (a quantitative association between TTP and a clinical outcome); `{r} n_distinct(es_mort$study_id)` of these reported mortality, contributing `{r} nrow(es_mort)` effect sizes. The **sensitivity pool** adds studies that met only the inclusive criterion (TTP and a clinical outcome both reported in the same cohort, not necessarily cross-tabulated); it comprises `{r} nrow(tbl_study)` studies in total, `{r} n_distinct(es_inc$study_id)` of which contribute `{r} nrow(es_inc)` mortality effect sizes.

# 2. Included studies

## 2.1 Study characteristics

```{r}
#| label: tbl-studies
#| tbl-cap: "Characteristics of all studies in the extraction workbook (primary and inclusive-only). N is the sum of participants across extracted arms. Pathogen: GN, Gram-negative; GP, Gram-positive; F, fungal; M, mixed or polymicrobial. Outcomes: M, mortality; PB, persistent bacteremia; MC, microbiological clearance; R, relapse; O, other clinical outcome. RoB, overall QUIPS risk of bias."
path_abbr <- c(gram_negative = "GN", gram_positive = "GP", fungal = "F", mixed = "M")
out_abbr <- function(x) {
  grp <- case_when(
    x == "mortality" | grepl("mortality", x) ~ "M",
    x == "persistent_bacteremia"             ~ "PB",
    x %in% c("microbiological_clearance", "bacteremia_clearance") ~ "MC",
    x == "relapse"                           ~ "R",
    TRUE                                     ~ "O")
  paste(intersect(c("M", "PB", "MC", "R", "O"), unique(grp)), collapse = ", ")
}

pop_sum <- tbl_pop |>
  group_by(study_id) |>
  summarise(
    N = if (all(is.na(n_total))) NA_real_ else sum(n_total, na.rm = TRUE),
    Pathogen = paste(unique(na.omit(path_abbr[pathogen_class])), collapse = ", "),
    .groups = "drop")
out_sum <- tbl_out |> group_by(study_id) |> summarise(Outcomes = out_abbr(outcome_type), .groups = "drop")
cut_sum <- tbl_ttp |>
  group_by(study_id) |>
  summarise(Cutpoint = if (all(is.na(ttp_cutpoint_hours))) "" else {
    r <- range(ttp_cutpoint_hours, na.rm = TRUE)
    if (r[1] == r[2]) format(r[1]) else paste(format(r[1]), format(r[2]), sep = "-") },
    .groups = "drop")

studies_tbl <- tbl_study |>
  left_join(pop_sum, by = "study_id") |>
  left_join(out_sum, by = "study_id") |>
  left_join(cut_sum, by = "study_id") |>
  mutate(Pool = if_else(grepl("[INCLUSIVE_ONLY]", coalesce(notes, ""), fixed = TRUE),
                        "Inclusive", "Primary")) |>
  arrange(factor(Pool, c("Primary", "Inclusive")), first_author, pub_year)

studies_tbl |>
  transmute(
    Study = study_label(study_id, first_author, pub_year),
    Country = country,
    Design = str_replace_all(study_design, "_", " "),
    N = ifelse(is.na(N), "NR", fmt_n(N)),
    Pathogen,
    Outcomes,
    `Cut-point (h)` = Cutpoint,
    RoB = str_to_title(rob_overall),
    Pool) |>
  tab(w = c(3.4, 1.5, 1.8, .8, 1, 1.3, 1.1, 1.1, 1.1))
```

Pool: Primary, strict criterion (`{r} sum(studies_tbl$Pool == "Primary")` studies); Inclusive, meets only the inclusive criterion (`{r} sum(studies_tbl$Pool == "Inclusive")` studies). NR, not reported. Cutpoint is the TTP threshold (hours) used to define short versus long TTP, given as a range when a study reported several.

## 2.2 Summary of included studies

```{r}
#| label: tbl-studies-summary
#| tbl-cap: "Summary of study-level characteristics by analysis pool."
sm <- studies_tbl |>
  mutate(Design = str_replace_all(study_design, "_", " "),
         RoB = factor(rob_overall, levels = c("low", "moderate", "high", "critical")))
bind_rows(
  sm |> count(Pool, Level = Design) |> mutate(Characteristic = "Design"),
  sm |> count(Pool, Level = as.character(RoB)) |> mutate(Characteristic = "Risk of bias (QUIPS)"),
  sm |> mutate(Level = as.character(cut(pub_year, c(-Inf, 2009, 2014, 2019, Inf),
                                        labels = c("2009 or earlier", "2010-2014", "2015-2019", "2020 or later")))) |>
    count(Pool, Level) |> mutate(Characteristic = "Publication year")
) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = Pool, values_from = n, values_fill = 0) |>
  mutate(Total = Primary + Inclusive) |>
  select(Characteristic, Level, Primary, Inclusive, Total) |>
  tab()
```

## 2.3 Mortality effect sizes

```{r}
#| label: tbl-es-mortality
#| tbl-cap: "Mortality effect sizes in the primary pool (short versus long TTP). Source: 2x2, computed from event counts; Rep-adj and Rep-unadj, back-calculated from a reported adjusted or unadjusted OR, HR, or RR with 95% CI. Time is the outcome time point in days. OR is exp(yi) with a Wald 95% CI."
src_abbr <- c(two_by_two = "2x2", reported_adjusted = "Rep-adj", reported_unadjusted = "Rep-unadj",
              continuous_per_hour = "Per-hour")
es_mort |>
  left_join(select(tbl_study, study_id, first_author), by = "study_id") |>
  arrange(first_author, pub_year, study_id, arm_id) |>
  transmute(
    Study = study_label(study_id, first_author, pub_year),
    Arm = arm_id,
    `Time (d)` = outcome_timepoint_days,
    Source = unname(src_abbr[es_source]),
    Pathogen = coalesce(unname(path_abbr[pathogen_class]), ""),
    `Cut-point (h)` = ifelse(is.na(ttp_cutpoint_hours), "", format(ttp_cutpoint_hours)),
    `OR (95% CI)` = sprintf("%.2f (%.2f to %.2f)", exp(yi), exp(yi - qnorm(.975) * sei), exp(yi + qnorm(.975) * sei))) |>
  tab(w = c(3.2, 1, 1, 1.2, 1, 1.2, 2.2))
```

# 3. Model specification

All pooled and moderator models were Bayesian random-effects models fitted with `brms`: $y_i \mid \mathrm{SE}_i \sim \mathcal{N}(\mu + u_s,\ \mathrm{SE}_i^2)$ with study-level random intercepts $u_s \sim \mathcal{N}(0, \tau^2)$, where $y_i$ is the log odds ratio for effect size $i$ and $\mathrm{SE}_i$ its standard error. Priors were $\mu \sim \mathcal{N}(0, 1)$, $\tau \sim \text{Half-Cauchy}(0, 0.5)$, and $\mathcal{N}(0, 0.5)$ for moderator coefficients. Each model used 4 chains of 4,000 iterations (1,000 warm-up; 12,000 post-warm-up draws), `adapt_delta = 0.99`, and `max_treedepth = 12`. The persistent bacteremia and microbiological clearance models were fitted with the CmdStan backend and all others with rstan. The 95% prediction interval for a new study is the central 95% interval of the predictive distribution $\mathcal{N}(\mu, \tau^2)$. $I^2$ was computed per posterior draw as $\tau^2 / (\tau^2 + \bar{v})$, where $\bar{v}$ is the mean within-study variance. Code is in `R/02_fit_models.R` and the analysis notebooks.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-model-list
#| tbl-cap: "Fitted models. k is the number of effect sizes and Studies the number of distinct studies in each model."
model_desc <- tribble(
  ~name,                 ~Description,
  "fit_base",            "Overall pooled effect, mortality",
  "fit_gram_pos",        "Pooled effect, Gram-positive subgroup",
  "fit_gram_neg",        "Pooled effect, Gram-negative subgroup",
  "fit_fungal",          "Pooled effect, fungal subgroup",
  "fit_metareg",         "Pathogen class meta-regression (Gram-positive vs Gram-negative)",
  "fit_cutpoint",        "TTP cutpoint meta-regression (2x2 effect sizes; cutpoint centered at median)",
  "fit_cutpoint_le24",   "TTP cutpoint meta-regression restricted to cutpoints of 24 h or less",
  "fit_gneg_cutpoint",   "TTP cutpoint meta-regression, Gram-negative effect sizes",
  "fit_gpos_cutpoint",   "TTP cutpoint meta-regression, Gram-positive effect sizes",
  "fit_gpos_cutpoint_sens", "Gram-positive cutpoint meta-regression excluding Minejima 2019 (72 h)",
  "fit_2x2",             "Pooled effect, 2x2-derived effect sizes only",
  "fit_reported",        "Pooled effect, reported (back-calculated) effect sizes only",
  "fit_es_source",       "Effect-size source meta-regression (2x2 as reference)",
  "fit_adjustment",      "Adjusted vs unadjusted reported estimates",
  "fit_year",            "Publication year meta-regression (centered at median)",
  "fit_pb",              "Pooled effect, persistent bacteremia",
  "fit_pb_defgroup",     "Persistent bacteremia by outcome-definition group",
  "fit_clr",             "Pooled effect, microbiological clearance")
prim_files <- sub("\\.rds$", "", list.files(prim_dir, pattern = "\\.rds$"))
model_desc |>
  filter(name %in% prim_files) |>
  mutate(fit = map(name, read_fit),
         Formula = map_chr(fit, \(f) paste(deparse(formula(f)$formula), collapse = "")),
         k = map_int(fit, \(f) nrow(f$data)),
         Studies = map_int(fit, \(f) n_distinct(f$data$study_id))) |>
  select(Model = name, Description, Formula, k, Studies) |>
  tab(w = c(2.2, 4.5, 4.3, .6, .9))
```

# 4. Model fit, diagnostics, and convergence

## 4.1 Posterior summaries of the pooled models

```{r}
#| label: tbl-pooled-fit
#| tbl-cap: "Posterior summaries of the pooled random-effects models. OR is the posterior median odds ratio (short versus long TTP) with its 95% credible interval; PI is the 95% prediction interval for a new study; tau is the between-study SD of the log-OR; I2 is the posterior median; P(OR > 1) is the posterior probability of an association in the direction of harm."
pooled_row <- function(name, label, dir = prim_dir) {
  if (!file.exists(fit_path(name, dir))) return(NULL)
  f <- read_fit(name, dir); p <- pooled_summary(f)
  tibble(Model = label,
         k = nrow(f$data), Studies = n_distinct(f$data$study_id),
         OR = sprintf("%.2f (%.2f to %.2f)", p$median_OR, p$ci_OR[1], p$ci_OR[2]),
         PI = sprintf("%.2f to %.2f", p$pi_OR[1], p$pi_OR[2]),
         tau = sprintf("%.2f", p$median_tau),
         I2 = sprintf("%.0f%%", p$median_i2),
         `P(OR > 1)` = sprintf("%.1f%%", 100 * p$p_harm))
}
bind_rows(
  pooled_row("fit_base",     "Mortality, all (primary)"),
  pooled_row("fit_gram_neg", "Mortality, Gram-negative"),
  pooled_row("fit_gram_pos", "Mortality, Gram-positive"),
  pooled_row("fit_fungal",   "Mortality, fungal"),
  pooled_row("fit_2x2",      "Mortality, 2x2 only"),
  pooled_row("fit_reported", "Mortality, reported only"),
  pooled_row("fit_pb",       "Persistent bacteremia"),
  pooled_row("fit_clr",      "Microbiological clearance"),
  pooled_row("fit_base",     "Mortality, all (sensitivity pool)", sens_dir)
) |> tab()
```

The microbiological clearance model rests on 4 effect sizes from 3 studies, so its between-study SD, and therefore its prediction interval, is essentially unconstrained by the data and the interval should not be interpreted.

## 4.2 Convergence across all fitted models

```{r}
#| label: tbl-conv-all
#| tbl-cap: "Convergence diagnostics for every fitted model. Parameters are population-level effects and the between-study SD; study-level random effects are not summarized. Treedepth hits count post-warm-up iterations that reached the maximum tree depth of 12."
conv_row <- function(path, pool) {
  fit <- readRDS(path)
  d <- summarise_draws(as_draws_df(fit), rhat = rhat, ess_bulk = ess_bulk, ess_tail = ess_tail) |>
    filter(!grepl("^lp__|^lprior|^Intercept$|^r_study_id|^z_", variable))
  np <- nuts_params(fit)
  tibble(Model = sub("\\.rds$", "", basename(path)), Pool = pool,
         `Max R-hat` = sprintf("%.3f", max(d$rhat, na.rm = TRUE)),
         `Min bulk ESS` = sprintf("%.0f", min(d$ess_bulk, na.rm = TRUE)),
         `Min tail ESS` = sprintf("%.0f", min(d$ess_tail, na.rm = TRUE)),
         `Divergent transitions` = sum(np$Value[np$Parameter == "divergent__"]),
         `Treedepth hits` = sum(np$Value[np$Parameter == "treedepth__"] >= 12))
}
conv_tbl <- bind_rows(
  map(list.files(prim_dir, full.names = TRUE, pattern = "\\.rds$"), conv_row, pool = "Primary"),
  map(list.files(sens_dir, full.names = TRUE, pattern = "\\.rds$"), conv_row, pool = "Sensitivity"))
tab(conv_tbl, w = c(2.6, 1.3, 1, 1.1, 1.1, 1.3, 1.1))
n_div     <- sum(conv_tbl$`Divergent transitions`)
max_rhat  <- max(as.numeric(conv_tbl$`Max R-hat`))
min_ess   <- min(as.numeric(conv_tbl$`Min bulk ESS`))
min_tail  <- min(as.numeric(conv_tbl$`Min tail ESS`))
div_models <- paste(unique(paste0(conv_tbl$Model, " (", tolower(conv_tbl$Pool), ")")[conv_tbl$`Divergent transitions` > 0]), collapse = ", ")
```

Across `{r} nrow(conv_tbl)` fitted models the maximum $\hat{R}$ was `{r} sprintf("%.3f", max_rhat)`, the minimum bulk ESS was `{r} fmt_n(min_ess)`, and the minimum tail ESS was `{r} fmt_n(min_tail)`. `{r} if (n_div == 0) "No divergent transitions occurred." else paste0("Divergent transitions occurred in ", n_div, " post-warm-up draws in total, confined to: ", div_models, ". Estimates from models with divergent transitions, which have few effect sizes, should be interpreted cautiously.")`

## 4.3 Primary pool: pooled model

```{r}
#| label: tbl-diag
#| tbl-cap: "Convergence diagnostics for the primary pooled model (all mortality effect sizes)."
fit_prim <- read_fit("fit_base")
summarise_draws(as_draws_df(fit_prim), rhat = rhat, ess_bulk = ess_bulk, ess_tail = ess_tail) |>
  filter(!grepl("^lp__|^lprior|^Intercept$|^r_study_id|^z_|^sigma$", variable)) |>
  transmute(Parameter = variable, `R-hat` = sprintf("%.3f", rhat),
            `Bulk ESS` = sprintf("%.0f", ess_bulk), `Tail ESS` = sprintf("%.0f", ess_tail)) |>
  tab()
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-trace
#| fig-cap: "Trace plots for the mean (mu) and between-study SD (tau) of the primary pooled model. Well-mixed, overlapping chains indicate good convergence."
#| fig-width: 6.5
#| fig-height: 5
bayesplot::mcmc_trace(
  fit_prim, pars = c("b_Intercept", "sd_study_id__Intercept"),
  facet_args = list(ncol = 1, labeller = as_labeller(c(
    b_Intercept = "mu (pooled log-OR)", sd_study_id__Intercept = "tau (between-study SD)")))) +
  theme_jama(base_size = 10)
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-rank
#| fig-cap: "Rank plots for the primary pooled model. Uniform histograms across chains indicate good mixing."
#| fig-width: 6.5
#| fig-height: 3.5
bayesplot::mcmc_rank_overlay(fit_prim, pars = c("b_Intercept", "sd_study_id__Intercept")) +
  theme_jama(base_size = 10)
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-rhat
#| fig-cap: "Distribution of R-hat across all parameters of the primary pooled model, including study-level random effects (dashed line at 1.01)."
#| fig-width: 6.5
#| fig-height: 3
rhat_prim <- summarise_draws(fit_prim, rhat = rhat) |>
  filter(!grepl("^lp__|^lprior", variable)) |> (\(d) setNames(d$rhat, d$variable))()
bayesplot::mcmc_rhat_hist(rhat_prim, binwidth = 0.0005) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 1.01, linetype = "dashed", color = jama_ref_line) +
  theme_jama(base_size = 10)
```

## 4.4 Posterior predictive check and cross-validation

```{r}
#| label: fig-ppc
#| fig-cap: "Posterior predictive check for the primary pooled model: observed log odds ratios (dark line) against 50 replicated data sets drawn from the posterior (light lines)."
#| fig-width: 6.5
#| fig-height: 3.5
# Observation-level SEs are fixed in the model, so replicates use each effect size's own SE
brms::pp_check(fit_prim, type = "dens_overlay", ndraws = 50) +
  labs(x = "Log odds ratio") + theme_jama(base_size = 10)
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-loo
#| tbl-cap: "Leave-one-out cross-validation (PSIS-LOO) for the pooled models. Pareto k above 0.7 means the importance-sampling approximation is unreliable for that effect size. Many effect sizes exceed this threshold, as is typical when each study has its own random intercept, so the ELPD values are reported for completeness and should not be used to compare models."
loo_row <- function(name, label, dir) {
  l <- suppressWarnings(brms::loo(read_fit(name, dir)))
  k <- loo::pareto_k_values(l)
  tibble(Model = label, Observations = length(k),
         `ELPD (SE)` = sprintf("%.1f (%.1f)", l$estimates["elpd_loo", "Estimate"], l$estimates["elpd_loo", "SE"]),
         `Effective parameters` = sprintf("%.1f", l$estimates["p_loo", "Estimate"]),
         `Pareto k > 0.7` = sum(k > 0.7),
         `Max Pareto k` = sprintf("%.2f", max(k)))
}
bind_rows(
  loo_row("fit_base", "Mortality, all (primary)", prim_dir),
  loo_row("fit_base", "Mortality, all (sensitivity pool)", sens_dir)) |>
  tab()
```

# 5. Sensitivity analyses

## 5.1 Adding the inclusive-only studies

```{r}
#| label: tbl-sens-pool
#| tbl-cap: "Pooled odds ratios for mortality in the primary pool (strict criterion) and the sensitivity pool (strict plus inclusive-only studies). Subgroup models are those defined in Section 2."
pool_pair <- function(name, label) {
  bind_rows(pooled_row(name, label) |> mutate(Pool = "Primary"),
            pooled_row(name, label, sens_dir) |> mutate(Pool = "Sensitivity"))
}
bind_rows(
  pool_pair("fit_base",     "All mortality"),
  pool_pair("fit_gram_neg", "Gram-negative"),
  pool_pair("fit_gram_pos", "Gram-positive"),
  pool_pair("fit_fungal",   "Fungal"),
  pool_pair("fit_2x2",      "2x2 only"),
  pool_pair("fit_reported", "Reported only")) |>
  select(Model, Pool, k, Studies, OR, PI, tau, I2) |>
  tab()
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-sens-pool
#| fig-cap: "Posterior densities of the pooled odds ratio in the primary pool and the sensitivity pool (inclusive-only studies added)."
#| fig-width: 6.5
#| fig-height: 3.5
bind_rows(
  tibble(OR = pooled_summary(fit_prim)$OR_draws, Pool = sprintf("Primary (%d studies)", n_distinct(es_mort$study_id))),
  tibble(OR = pooled_summary(fit_sens)$OR_draws, Pool = sprintf("Sensitivity (%d studies)", n_distinct(es_inc$study_id)))) |>
  ggplot(aes(OR, fill = Pool)) +
  geom_density(alpha = 0.55) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 1, linetype = "dashed", color = jama_ref_line) +
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0.5, 5)) +
  scale_fill_jama() +
  labs(x = "Pooled OR (short vs long TTP)", y = "Posterior density") +
  theme_jama(base_size = 10) + theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

## 5.2 Effect-size derivation

```{r}
#| label: tbl-es-source
#| tbl-cap: "Pooled odds ratio by effect-size source (separate random-effects models)."
src_post <- bind_rows(pooled_row("fit_2x2", "2x2-derived only"), pooled_row("fit_reported", "Reported only (adjusted and unadjusted)")) |>
  select(Model, k, Studies, OR, tau, I2)
tab(src_post)

```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-es-contrast
#| tbl-cap: "Contrasts from the joint effect-size-source meta-regression, with 2x2-derived effect sizes as the reference. A positive difference in log-OR means the reported estimates show a larger short-TTP association than the 2x2 estimates."
d_src <- as_draws_df(read_fit("fit_es_source"))
contr <- function(pat, label) {
  b <- d_src[[grep(pat, names(d_src), value = TRUE)[1]]]
  tibble(Contrast = label, `Difference in log-OR` = sprintf("%+.3f", median(b)),
         `95% CrI` = sprintf("%+.3f to %+.3f", quantile(b, .025), quantile(b, .975)),
         `P(difference > 0)` = sprintf("%.1f%%", 100 * mean(b > 0)))
}
bind_rows(contr("reported_adjusted", "Reported (adjusted) vs 2x2"),
          contr("reported_unadjusted", "Reported (unadjusted) vs 2x2")) |>
  tab()
```

## 5.3 TTP cutpoint analyses

```{r}
#| label: tbl-cutpoint
#| tbl-cap: "Change in the log odds ratio per additional hour of TTP cutpoint across cutpoint meta-regressions. P(slope < 0) is the posterior probability that higher cutpoints are associated with weaker associations."
slope_row <- function(name, label) {
  f <- read_fit(name); d <- as_draws_df(f)
  b <- d[[grep("^b_cutpoint_c$", names(d), value = TRUE)[1]]]
  tibble(Model = label, k = nrow(f$data), Studies = n_distinct(f$data$study_id),
         `Slope per hour` = sprintf("%.3f", median(b)),
         `95% CrI` = sprintf("%.3f to %.3f", quantile(b, .025), quantile(b, .975)),
         `P(slope < 0)` = sprintf("%.1f%%", 100 * mean(b < 0)))
}
bind_rows(
  slope_row("fit_cutpoint",            "All cutpoints"),
  slope_row("fit_cutpoint_le24",       "Cutpoints of 24 h or less"),
  slope_row("fit_gneg_cutpoint",       "Gram-negative"),
  slope_row("fit_gpos_cutpoint",       "Gram-positive"),
  slope_row("fit_gpos_cutpoint_sens",  "Gram-positive, excluding Minejima 2019 (72 h)")) |>
  tab()
```

## 5.4 Moderators

```{r}
#| label: tbl-mods
#| tbl-cap: "Moderator meta-regressions (primary pool). The difference in log-OR is the change in the pooled log-OR per unit of the moderator; negative values shrink the short-TTP association."
mod_row <- function(name, label, scale = 1, dir = "<") {
  d <- as_draws_df(read_fit(name))
  b <- d[[grep("^b_(?!Intercept)", names(d), perl = TRUE)[1]]]
  tibble(Moderator = label, `Difference in log-OR` = sprintf("%.3f", median(b) * scale),
         `95% CrI` = sprintf("%.3f to %.3f", quantile(b, .025) * scale, quantile(b, .975) * scale),
         `P(direction)` = sprintf("%s %.1f%%", if (dir == "<") "P(< 0)" else "P(> 0)",
                                  100 * if (dir == "<") mean(b < 0) else mean(b > 0)))
}
bind_rows(
  mod_row("fit_cutpoint",   "TTP cutpoint (per 10 h)", scale = 10),
  mod_row("fit_metareg",    "Pathogen: Gram-positive vs Gram-negative"),
  mod_row("fit_adjustment", "Adjusted vs unadjusted estimate", dir = ">"),
  mod_row("fit_year",       "Publication year (per 5 years)", scale = 5)) |>
  tab()
```

## 5.5 Small-study effects

```{r}
#| label: tbl-pubbias
#| tbl-cap: "Publication bias and small-study analyses for mortality (primary pool). These frequentist methods treat all effect sizes as independent and have limited reliability when heterogeneity is high."
rma_mort <- metafor::rma(yi = yi, sei = sei, data = es_mort, method = "REML")
egger <- metafor::regtest(rma_mort, model = "lm")
begg  <- metafor::ranktest(rma_mort)
tf    <- metafor::trimfill(rma_mort)
tibble(
  Analysis = c("Frequentist random-effects pooled OR (REML)",
               "Egger regression test",
               "Egger limit estimate as SE approaches 0 (OR)",
               "Begg rank correlation test",
               "Trim-and-fill: imputed studies",
               "Trim-and-fill adjusted OR"),
  Result = c(
    sprintf("%.2f (%.2f to %.2f)", exp(rma_mort$beta[1]), exp(rma_mort$ci.lb), exp(rma_mort$ci.ub)),
    sprintf("t = %.2f, df = %.0f, p %s", egger$zval, egger$ddf,
            ifelse(egger$pval < 1e-4, "< 0.0001", sprintf("= %.4f", egger$pval))),
    sprintf("%.2f (%.2f to %.2f)", exp(egger$est), exp(egger$ci.lb), exp(egger$ci.ub)),
    sprintf("Kendall tau = %.2f, p = %.2f", begg$tau, begg$pval),
    sprintf("%d", tf$k0),
    sprintf("%.2f (%.2f to %.2f)", exp(tf$beta[1]), exp(tf$ci.lb), exp(tf$ci.ub)))) |>
  tab()
```

## 5.6 Prior sensitivity

The primary mortality model was refitted to the same `{r} nrow(es_mort)` effect sizes with alternative priors, changing one prior at a time. Two alternatives change the prior on the between-study SD ($\tau$): a half-normal prior that puts less weight on large values, and a wider half-Cauchy prior. Two change the prior on the pooled log odds ratio ($\mu$): a vague prior, and a skeptical prior centered on no association that gives 95% prior probability to an odds ratio between 0.5 and 2.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-prior-sens
#| tbl-cap: "Prior sensitivity of the primary mortality model. The first row is the primary analysis (mu ~ Normal(0, 1), tau ~ Half-Cauchy(0, 0.5)); each other row changes one prior. Columns are as in the posterior summary table in section 4.1."
prior_fits <- fit_prior_sensitivity(es_mort)
sens_row <- function(fit, label) {
  p <- pooled_summary(fit)
  tibble(Analysis = label, k = nrow(fit$data), Studies = n_distinct(fit$data$study_id),
         OR = sprintf("%.2f (%.2f to %.2f)", p$median_OR, p$ci_OR[1], p$ci_OR[2]),
         PI = sprintf("%.2f to %.2f", p$pi_OR[1], p$pi_OR[2]),
         tau = sprintf("%.2f", p$median_tau),
         I2 = sprintf("%.0f%%", p$median_i2),
         `P(OR > 1)` = sprintf("%.1f%%", 100 * p$p_harm))
}
prior_tbl <- bind_rows(
  sens_row(fit_prim, "Primary priors"),
  map2_dfr(prior_fits, names(prior_fits), \(f, nm) sens_row(f, prior_specs[[nm]]$label)))
tab(prior_tbl, w = c(4, .6, .9, 2, 1.6, .7, .7, 1.1))
prior_or <- vapply(c(list(fit_prim), prior_fits), \(f) pooled_summary(f)$median_OR, 0)
```

Across the five prior specifications the pooled odds ratio ranged from `{r} sprintf("%.2f", min(prior_or))` to `{r} sprintf("%.2f", max(prior_or))`. The skeptical prior gave the smallest estimate, as expected for a prior centered on no association.

## 5.7 Risk of bias and adjustment

The primary model was refitted, with the primary priors, to three subsets of the mortality effect sizes: studies rated at low overall risk of bias (QUIPS); studies at low or moderate risk of bias (excluding those rated high or critical); and effect sizes back-calculated from adjusted reported estimates only.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-subset-sens
#| tbl-cap: "Pooled odds ratio for mortality restricted by risk of bias and by adjustment status, compared with the primary analysis. Columns are as in the posterior summary table in section 4.1."
subset_fits <- fit_subset_sensitivity(es_mort)
subset_tbl <- bind_rows(
  sens_row(fit_prim, "All effect sizes (primary)"),
  map2_dfr(subset_fits, names(subset_fits), \(f, nm) sens_row(f, subset_specs[[nm]]$label)))
tab(subset_tbl, w = c(4, .6, .9, 2, 1.6, .7, .7, 1.1))
```

These subsets are small, especially the low-risk-of-bias and adjusted-only subsets, so their credible intervals are wider than the primary interval. The adjusted-only subset is the closest available approximation to the independent prognostic association of TTP, but its estimates were adjusted for different covariate sets.

# 7. R packages

All analyses were run in R `{r} paste(R.version$major, R.version$minor, sep = ".")` with Quarto `{r} tryCatch(system2("quarto", "--version", stdout = TRUE)[1], error = \(e) "(version not found)")` for rendering. The table below lists the R packages that the analysis code calls directly, plus the Stan interface packages that `brms` uses to fit the models. Versions are those recorded in the project lockfile (`renv.lock`), which also lists every indirect dependency; `renv::restore()` reinstalls them.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-packages
#| tbl-cap: "R packages used in the analysis, with the versions recorded in `renv.lock`."
pkg_roles <- tribble(
  ~Package,      ~Use,
  "brms",        "Bayesian random-effects models and meta-regressions",
  "rstan",       "Stan backend for brms (all mortality models)",
  "StanHeaders", "Stan C++ headers used by rstan",
  "RcppParallel","Threading library used by rstan (version 5.1.x required)",
  "cmdstanr",    "CmdStan backend for brms (persistent bacteremia, clearance and relapse models)",
  "posterior",   "Posterior draws and convergence diagnostics",
  "loo",         "Leave-one-out cross-validation",
  "bayesplot",   "Trace, rank and posterior predictive plots",
  "metafor",     "Effect-size calculation and frequentist meta-analysis (Egger, Begg, trim-and-fill)",
  "lme4",        "Mixed-effects logistic regression (dose-response analysis)",
  "MASS",        "Multivariate normal simulation (dose-response analysis)",
  "readxl",      "Reading the extraction workbook",
  "tidyverse",   "Data manipulation (with dplyr, tidyr, purrr, stringr and readr)",
  "dplyr",       "Data manipulation",
  "tidyr",       "Data reshaping",
  "purrr",       "Iteration",
  "stringr",     "String handling",
  "readr",       "Reading and writing text files",
  "withr",       "Seeded random-number generation for prediction intervals",
  "ggplot2",     "Graphics",
  "ggdist",      "Posterior density and interval plots",
  "patchwork",   "Combining plots",
  "scales",      "Axis and label formatting",
  "gt",          "HTML tables in the analysis notebooks",
  "PRISMA2020",  "PRISMA 2020 flow diagram",
  "knitr",       "Executing code chunks and formatting tables",
  "rmarkdown",   "Document rendering with knitr"
)
lock_pkgs <- jsonlite::read_json("renv.lock")$Packages
cited <- c("brms", "rstan", "metafor", "posterior", "loo", "lme4", "tidyverse", "PRISMA2020")
pkg_roles |>
  mutate(Version = vapply(Package, \(p) lock_pkgs[[p]]$Version %||% NA_character_, ""),
         .after = Package) |>
  mutate(Reference = ifelse(Package %in% cited, paste0("[@pkg_", Package, "]"), "")) |>
  tab(w = c(2, 1.2, 5, 1.5))
```

CmdStan `{r} tryCatch(as.character(cmdstanr::cmdstan_version()), error = \(e) "(not found)")` is installed outside R; see the project README for setup.
